title: Finite-duration non-slow-roll effects in inflationary production of ultralight vector dark matter
comment: 21 pages, 16 figures, accepted in PRD with DOI: https://doi.org/10.1103/3kl4-n737
summary: Inflationary production of ultralight vector dark matter can be amplified by a brief non-slow-roll phase, yet instantaneous mass transitions generate ultraviolet ringing and leave finite-time predictions unresolved. We replace the sharp transition with a smooth profile and derive the momentum-response kernel of the longitudinal mode. Finite duration preserves the infrared enhancement, suppresses modes that resolve the transition, and introduces a profile-dependent correction to the relic abundance. After fixing the dark matter abundance, the induced gravitational-wave signal retains an independent transverse-traceless source dependence, so abundance rescaling alone leaves residual profile information. Numerical mode evolution and radiation-era tensor integration support the finite-width treatment. Transition duration therefore links microscopic inflationary dynamics to ultralight vector abundance and its low-frequency gravitational-wave signal.

AI.tldr: This paper replaces the sharp (instantaneous) mass transition in inflationary ultralight vector dark matter production with a smooth finite-width profile. The authors derive the momentum-response kernel for the longitudinal mode, showing that finite duration preserves the infrared enhancement while suppressing modes that resolve the transition and introduces profile-dependent corrections to the relic abundance. After abundance normalization, the induced gravitational-wave signal retains residual profile information due to independent transverse-traceless source dependence. Numerical mode evolution and radiation-era tensor integration confirm the finite-width treatment.
AI.motivation: Instantaneous mass transitions in ultralight vector dark matter production generate ultraviolet ringing artifacts and leave finite-time predictions unresolved. A smooth transition profile is needed to obtain physically well-defined predictions for both the relic abundance and the subsequent gravitational-wave signal.
AI.method: The sharp transition is replaced with a smooth finite-width profile, and the momentum-response kernel of the longitudinal mode is derived analytically. Numerical mode evolution and radiation-era tensor integration are used to support the finite-width treatment and validate the analytic results.
AI.result: Finite transition duration preserves the infrared enhancement of production, suppresses modes that resolve the transition time scale, and yields a profile-dependent correction to the relic abundance. After fixing the abundance, the induced gravitational-wave signal retains residual profile dependence due to the independent transverse-traceless source, meaning abundance rescaling alone cannot eliminate profile information.
AI.conclusion: The transition duration connects microscopic inflationary dynamics to the ultralight vector relic abundance and its low-frequency gravitational-wave signature, providing a more realistic framework for predicting observational signals from such scenarios.

title: Resolving Local Structure of Distribution Functions in Collider Measurements
summary: Collider measurements may blur narrow features in underlying distributions before fitting, since a data point samples a finite region. We show that observables linear in a selected target distribution, after externally constrained inputs are absorbed into a nonnegative finite response, have a calculable distribution-space locality set by hard dynamics and kinematics. The baseline-normalized $F_{\rm dir}(X)$ yields the local value at zero width and a controlled average otherwise, with covariance setting the leading bias. This guides the choice of processes and observables that retain unexpected fine structure. An EIC photon-radiation observable realizes the exact zero-width limit.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that collider observables linear in a target distribution, with external inputs absorbed into a nonnegative finite response, possess a calculable distribution-space locality set by hard dynamics and kinematics. The baseline-normalized observable F_dir(X) provides a controlled average with covariance setting the leading bias, guiding the selection of processes that preserve unexpected fine structure, with an EIC photon-radiation observable achieving the exact zero-width limit.
AI.motivation: Collider measurements inevitably blur narrow features in underlying distributions due to finite detector/phase-space resolution before fitting. Understanding the intrinsic locality of observables in distribution space is crucial for knowing whether fine structure can be resolved, motivating a framework to quantify this limitation and identify observables that retain such features.
AI.method: The authors analyze observables that are linear functionals of a selected target distribution, incorporating externally constrained inputs absorbed into a nonnegative finite response kernel. They demonstrate that the resulting distribution-space locality is calculable from hard dynamics and kinematics. They define the baseline-normalized F_dir(X) which evaluates the local value at zero width and yields a controlled average otherwise, with the covariance determining the leading systematic bias.
AI.result: The framework produces a calculable locality bound for collider observables. The baseline-normalized observable F_dir(X) provides local extraction at zero width and achieves controlled averaging at finite width. An explicit EIC photon-radiation observable is identified that realizes the exact zero-width limit, thereby enabling undistorted measurement of fine structure.
AI.conclusion: The analysis establishes a principled criterion for selecting collider processes and observables that can retain unexpected fine structure, with covariance-based leading-bias control, and demonstrates a concrete EIC photon-radiation observable as an exact zero-width realization.

title: Probing Quantum Foundations in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillations: Wave Packet Approach from MINOS Data to DUNE Predictions
summary: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the wave packet formalism, extending the standard planewave treatment to incorporate the finite spatial coherence of neutrino mass eigenstates.We derive the full three flavor oscillation probability with MSW matter effects, decoherence, and localization suppression governed by the wave packet width, benchmarking against MINOS disappearance data and extending to DUNE predictions under the same parameters. To quantify how sharply the oscillation data constrain the wave packet width, we compute the classical Fisher information FC as a function of neutrino energy for both MINOS and DUNE, and show that its sensitivity is concentrated precisely in the low-energy regime where the wave-packet and plane-wave predictions diverge. Beyond the oscillation probability analysis, we compute wave particle entanglement complementarity quantities within a quantum information theoretic framework and explore the complete triality description involving entanglement, predictability, and visibility as functions of neutrino energy for both experiments such as MINOS and DUNE. We show that even when the oscillation probability is numerically indistinguishable from the planewave result, the wave packet structure leaves observable imprints in these triality measures. Our results demonstrate that the wave packet approach provides a theoretically consistent and experimentally motivated framework for probing quantum foundations in long-baseline atmospheric neutrino oscillation experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper extends neutrino flavor oscillation analysis to the wave packet formalism, incorporating finite spatial coherence of neutrino mass eigenstates. It derives the full three-flavor oscillation probability with MSW matter effects, decoherence, and localization suppression, benchmarking against MINOS data and predicting for DUNE. Using Fisher information, it shows the wave packet width sensitivity is concentrated in the low-energy regime where wave-packet and plane-wave predictions diverge. Additionally, the authors compute wave-particle entanglement complementarity (triality) measures and show these leave observable imprints even when oscillation probabilities are numerically indistinguishable from the plane-wave result.
AI.motivation: To provide a theoretically consistent framework beyond the standard plane-wave treatment for neutrino oscillations, incorporating the finite spatial coherence of mass eigenstates, and to explore whether quantum information theoretic measures can reveal wave packet structure that standard oscillation probabilities cannot distinguish.
AI.method: The authors employ a wave packet formalism for neutrinos, deriving three-flavor oscillation probabilities with MSW matter effects and decoherence/localization suppression from wave packet width. They use classical Fisher information to quantify parameter sensitivity as a function of neutrino energy, and compute quantum information theoretic triality measures (entanglement, predictability, visibility) for both MINOS and DUNE experiments.
AI.result: Fisher information sensitivity to the wave packet width is concentrated in the low-energy regime where wave-packet and plane-wave predictions diverge. Even when oscillation probabilities are numerically indistinguishable from plane-wave results, the triality measures (entanglement, predictability, visibility) reveal observable imprints of the wave packet structure for both MINOS and DUNE.
AI.conclusion: The wave packet approach provides a theoretically consistent and experimentally motivated framework for probing quantum foundations in long-baseline atmospheric neutrino oscillation experiments, with triality quantities offering additional observables sensitive to quantum coherence effects.

title: Sub-TeV Singlino Dark Matter in light from Sagittarius A$^\ast$ and LUX-ZEPLIN Nuclear-Recoil Event
summary: We investigate the impact of a dark matter density spike surrounding the Milky Way's supermassive black hole (SMBH) on the detectability of Singlino-dominated neutralino dark matter within the Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (NMSSM). Similar density enhancements, or mini-spikes, around stellar-mass black holes (sBHs), have also been considered. Such a dark matter (DM) candidate typically produces weak indirect detection signals in conventional dark matter halos. Additionally, a Singlino-like lightest supersymmetric particle (LSP) is very difficult to probe at the LHC or through the direct DM search experiments. On top of that, recent observation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Nuclear-Recoil Event may hint towards a DM that can be accommodated by a Singlino with mass more than 200 GeV. Keeping these in consideration, we examine the prospects for detecting these sub-TeV dark matter scenarios through gamma-ray observations of the regions surrounding the SMBH Sgr A$^\ast$ and the sBH in the low-mass X-ray binary XTE J1118+480.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether Singlino-dominated neutralino dark matter in the NMSSM, which is typically difficult to detect via conventional means, could be observable through gamma-ray emissions from dark matter density spikes around the Milky Way's supermassive black hole (Sgr A*) and stellar-mass black holes (e.g., in XTE J1118+480).
AI.motivation: Singlino-dominated LSP dark matter in the NMSSM produces weak indirect detection signals in standard halos and is difficult to probe at colliders or in direct detection experiments. The recent LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Nuclear-Recoil Event may hint at a Singlino DM candidate with mass >200 GeV, motivating exploration of alternative detection channels such as gamma-ray observations near black hole density spikes.
AI.method: The authors model dark matter density spikes (mini-spikes) around Sgr A* and stellar-mass black holes, and compute the gamma-ray signals arising from Singlino-dominated neutralino annihilation in the NMSSM for sub-TeV DM masses, assessing detectability against these enhanced density environments.
AI.result: The paper examines the detection prospects for sub-TeV Singlino dark matter scenarios via gamma-ray observations targeting the DM-enhanced regions around Sgr A* and the stellar-mass black hole in XTE J1118+480.
AI.conclusion: Density spikes around black holes may provide a viable avenue for probing otherwise elusive Singlino-dominated NMSSM dark matter through gamma-ray indirect detection.

title: Taxonomy of Potentials in Asymptotic Limits
summary:
In infinite-distance limits of scalar field moduli spaces in quantum gravity, particle masses, brane tensions, and scalar field potentials scale exponentially with geodesic distance. Previous work has shown that the exponential decay rates of particle masses and brane tensions admit a discrete classification. In this work, we extend this classification to the case of scalar field potentials. We find that leading contributions to the potential typically scale with tensions of codimension-1 branes as $V \sim T_{d-1}^2$ or codimension-0 branes as $V \sim T_d$, and these relations hold formally even when the associated branes are absent from the spectrum. As a result, the taxonomy rules for potentials are intimately connected to the brane taxonomy rules. More generally, potential contributions can be labeled by a collection of integers, which correspond physically to their transformation properties under Weyl rescalings and their order in the string loop expansion. This implies that the vector $\vec v = - \vec 
abla \log V$ is lattice-valued, and indeed it lies in precisely the same lattice as the analogous vectors $\vec α= - \vec 
abla \log T_d$ for codimension-0 branes of tension $T_d$. We verify our taxonomy rules in various examples in string theory. We show that these rules imply that sums of positive potential terms satisfy the Strong Asymptotic de Sitter Conjecture, which requires $|\vec 
abla \log V| \geq 2/\sqrt{d-2}$ in asymptotic regimes of scalar field moduli space, and they imply that higher-derivative gravitational corrections are suppressed by powers of the species scale.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the discrete classification of exponential decay rates in scalar field moduli spaces from particle masses and brane tensions to scalar field potentials, showing that leading potential contributions scale as brane tensions squared (codimension-1) or directly (codimension-0), with potential contributions labeled by integers corresponding to Weyl rescaling properties and string loop order, implying the potential gradient vector is lattice-valued and that sums of positive potential terms satisfy the Strong Asymptotic de Sitter Conjecture.
AI.motivation: Previous work classified exponential decay rates for particle masses and brane tensions in infinite-distance limits of scalar field moduli spaces in quantum gravity. This work aims to extend this classification to scalar field potentials, which is crucial for understanding the Swampland conjectures and the asymptotic structure of quantum gravity.
AI.method: The authors establish taxonomy rules connecting scalar field potential contributions to brane tensions: potentials scale as V ~ T_{d-1}^2 for codimension-1 branes or V ~ T_d for codimension-0 branes. They introduce integer labels for potential contributions corresponding to Weyl rescaling transformations and string loop order, demonstrating that the vector v = -∇ log V is lattice-valued and lies in the same lattice as α = -∇ log T_d for codimension-0 branes. The rules are verified in string theory examples.
AI.result: The taxonomy rules are verified in various string theory examples. The rules imply that sums of positive potential terms satisfy the Strong Asymptotic de Sitter Conjecture requiring |∇ log V| ≥ 2/√(d-2) in asymptotic regimes, and that higher-derivative gravitational corrections are suppressed by powers of the species scale. The relations between potentials and brane tensions hold formally even when the associated branes are absent from the spectrum.
AI.conclusion: The discrete classification of exponential decay rates extends naturally to scalar field potentials, connecting potential taxonomy intimately to brane taxonomy. The lattice-valued nature of potential gradient vectors and the resulting constraints (Strong Asymptotic dS Conjecture, species scale suppression) provide robust predictions for asymptotic quantum gravity regimes.

title: Yukawa coupling deviations from four-quark interactions
summary: New physics generating four-quark interactions can be difficult to detect at the LHC, especially if it does not couple to first generation quarks. We investigate the possible role of such interactions in generating measurable deviations in Higgs-quark couplings. We find important constraints from flavour physics and top-pair production, but show that Higgs-charm and Higgs-bottom couplings remain the most sensitive LHC observables to some four-quark operators involving scalar currents. At FCC-ee, more operators and flavour structures can be tested. We further investigate simple single-particle models that can generate these interactions, including a second Higgs doublet, and scalar and vector diquarks. We find that in some cases, including new scalars most strongly coupled to the third generation of quarks, deviations in Yukawa couplings could offer the first signs of new physics generating four-quark interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how new physics generating four-quark interactions—particularly those not coupling to first-generation quarks—can produce measurable deviations in Higgs-quark couplings. The authors find that flavour physics and top-pair production provide important constraints, but Higgs-charm and Higgs-bottom couplings are the most sensitive LHC observables for certain scalar-current four-quark operators. FCC-ee would extend sensitivity to more operators and flavour structures. Simple single-particle models (second Higgs doublet, scalar and vector diquarks) are examined, showing that new scalars most strongly coupled to the third generation could make Yukawa coupling deviations the first observable sign of this new physics.
AI.motivation: Four-quark interactions from new physics that do not couple to first-generation quarks are difficult to detect at the LHC using conventional searches. The paper aims to identify alternative observables—specifically Higgs-quark couplings—that could serve as sensitive probes of such hidden new physics.
AI.method: The authors analyze how four-quark operators with scalar currents can induce deviations in Higgs-charm and Higgs-bottom couplings. They examine constraints from flavour physics and top-pair production measurements, and compare LHC sensitivity with projected FCC-ee reach. They also construct and study simple ultraviolet-complete single-particle models—a second Higgs doublet as well as scalar and vector diquarks—to assess which scenarios yield observable Yukawa coupling deviations.
AI.result: Flavour physics and top-pair production impose important constraints, yet Higgs-charm and Higgs-bottom couplings remain the most sensitive LHC observables to scalar-current four-quark operators. FCC-ee would allow testing of additional operators and flavour structures. Certain single-particle models, particularly new scalars coupled strongly to the third generation of quarks, can produce Yukawa coupling deviations that may be the first detectable signature of four-quark new physics.
AI.conclusion: Higgs-quark coupling measurements—at the LHC and especially at FCC-ee—can serve as powerful indirect probes for four-quark new physics that evades direct detection. Third-generation-coupled scalar diquarks represent particularly compelling scenarios where Yukawa coupling deviations could be the leading observable signal.

title: Gravitational Backreaction in de Sitter: A Canonical ADM Approach
summary: We develop a canonical ADM framework for gravitational backreaction during inflation. Our approach extends the formalism used to compute cosmological correlators by applying it to the evolution of the quantum background, which we identify with the metric one-point function. The aim is to assess the quantum stability of inflationary geometries under gravitational backreaction. Within this framework, the backreaction is determined by the expectation values of the Hamiltonian constraint and the equations of motion for the spatial metric. Working in the exact de Sitter limit, we apply the framework to a massless minimally coupled spectator scalar field and the physical graviton polarizations. At one loop, their backreaction renormalizes the relation between the cosmological constant and the Hubble parameter without inducing any secular departure from de Sitter evolution, in agreement with previous results. We perform the calculation using a hard momentum cutoff and show that a fixed physical cutoff allows the homogeneous background equations to be renormalized with time- and background-independent coefficients, in contrast to a fixed comoving cutoff. Finally, we demonstrate that the explicit representation of the backreaction depends on the gauge condition imposed on the metric fluctuations, as well as on the background-fluctuation split. Nevertheless, these different representations are related by a gauge transformation and are therefore physically equivalent.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a canonical ADM (Arnowitt-Deser-Misner) framework for computing gravitational backreaction during inflation, by extending the formalism used for cosmological correlators to the evolution of the quantum background (identified with the metric one-point function). Applied to massless minimally coupled scalars and gravitons in exact de Sitter space, it shows at one loop that backreaction only renormalizes the cosmological constant–Hubble parameter relation without secular departures from de Sitter, demonstrates that a fixed physical cutoff (unlike a comoving one) permits time- and background-independent renormalization, and establishes that representations of backreaction differ under gauge choices and background-fluctuation splits but remain physically equivalent via gauge transformations.
AI.motivation: To assess the quantum stability of inflationary geometries under gravitational backreaction—specifically whether quantum fluctuations of matter and gravitons can destabilize de Sitter-like inflationary backgrounds over time.
AI.method: A canonical ADM framework is constructed that relates backreaction to expectation values of the Hamiltonian constraint and the spatial metric equations of motion. The quantum background is identified with the metric one-point function. Calculations are performed in the exact de Sitter limit at one loop for a massless minimally coupled spectator scalar and physical graviton polarizations, using both fixed physical and fixed comoving momentum cutoffs, with analysis of gauge and background-fluctuation split dependence.
AI.result: At one loop, the backreaction from both the scalar and graviton polarizations only renormalizes the relation between the cosmological constant and Hubble parameter, with no secular departure from de Sitter evolution. A fixed physical cutoff yields renormalized background equations with time- and background-independent coefficients, unlike a fixed comoving cutoff. The explicit backreaction representation depends on gauge and the background-fluctuation split, but different representations are related by gauge transformations and are physically equivalent.
AI.conclusion: The canonical ADM framework provides a consistent method for computing gravitational backreaction during inflation, confirming the quantum stability of de Sitter geometries at one loop in the cases studied. The choice of physical versus comoving cutoff is important for achieving a sensible renormalization, and gauge/split dependence is merely representational, not physical.

title: A Task Force on Strong Coupling Determinations from Event Shapes
comment: 27 pages, 8 figures, 1 table; summary of the first meeting (https://indico.cern.ch/e/asthrust2025) of the newly established CERN Task Force on "Strong Coupling Determinations from Event Shapes" (https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/LHCPhysics/StrongCouplingFromEventShapesTaskForce)
summary: The strong coupling constant $α_s$ is a fundamental parameter of the Standard Model. Its precise determination is essential for accurately predicting, studying, and understanding processes at the Large Hadron Collider and future experiments such as the Future Circular Collider. Event shape and correlator observables measured at electron-positron colliders provide one of the cleanest environments for extracting $α_s$, thanks to their sensitivity to $α_s$ and the availability of high-precision data from the Large Electron-Positron Collider. More broadly, such observables provide an ideal setting to develop and test our understanding of the perturbative and non-perturbative elements of Quantum Chromodynamics, which will underpin the field's precision and discovery frontiers for decades to come. Despite these advances, significant discrepancies persist between different determinations of $α_s$ from event shapes, both in the extracted central values and estimated uncertainties. This document motivates the establishment of a dedicated Task Force to coordinate a community-wide effort addressing these open questions. We report on the first two-day meeting held at CERN in November 2025, summarizing the scientific discussion and documenting the experimental analyses identified as priorities during the meeting, as well as the concrete list of tasks to be carried out by the theory community in preparation for future meetings.

AI.tldr: This document outlines the motivation and initial proceedings of a community Task Force established to address persistent discrepancies in determinations of the strong coupling constant α_s from event-shape and correlator observables at electron-positron colliders. It reports on the first two-day organizational meeting held at CERN in November 2025, listing prioritized experimental analyses and concrete theory tasks for future work.
AI.motivation: The strong coupling constant α_s is a fundamental Standard Model parameter essential for precision predictions at the LHC and future colliders. While e+e− event-shape and correlator observables offer one of the cleanest environments for extracting α_s—thanks to high-precision LEP data and sensitivity to α_s—significant discrepancies persist between different extraction results, both in central values and uncertainties. This motivates a coordinated community-wide effort to resolve these open questions.
AI.method: The paper documents the establishment of a dedicated Task Force to coordinate community-wide efforts. It reports on the first two-day meeting held at CERN in November 2025, summarizing the scientific discussions, identifying prioritized experimental analyses during the meeting, and outlining a concrete list of theory tasks to be carried out in preparation for subsequent meetings.
AI.result: The outcome includes a report of the first CERN-based Task Force meeting held in November 2025, with a documented set of prioritized experimental analyses and a concrete agenda of theory-side tasks identified for future work toward harmonizing α_s determinations.
AI.conclusion: A community-coordinated Task Force has been established to systematically address the long-standing discrepancies in α_s extractions from e+e− event shapes. The first meeting at CERN set the groundwork—identifying priority analyses and theory tasks—to advance both perturbative and non-perturbative QCD understanding, with implications for precision physics at present and future colliders.

title: From $Z$ to $a$: High-temperature relations, subleading semi-universality, and conformal anomalies
summary: The free energy of any CFT, $ \ln Z(β; ω_i)$, admits two expansions: high temperature ($β\rightarrow 0$) and fast rotation ($ω_i \rightarrow 1$). We demonstrate that locality of the thermal effective action forces $\ln Z$ to take a simple analytic form at all orders in the high temperature expansion, and further imposes an infinite number of sharp relations on the coefficients in this expansion. All are homogeneous, except at order $β^1$ due to the Weyl anomaly. From this, the $a$-anomaly can be extracted from the partition function. The relations resum in the fast-spinning expansion into differential equations in $β$ obeyed by the semi-universal limit and its corrections. We verify the relations in a variety of CFTs. We generalize to any even $d$, but find no similar relations at odd $d$.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that locality of the thermal effective action in any CFT forces the free energy partition function to take a simple analytic form at all orders in the high-temperature expansion, imposing infinite sharp homogeneous relations on its coefficients (with an exception at order β¹ due to the Weyl anomaly). These relations allow extraction of the a-anomaly and resum into differential equations in the fast-rotation limit. The results generalize to even dimensions but fail in odd dimensions.
AI.motivation: To understand and constrain the structure of the CFT partition function on a thermal background (S¹ × S^{d-1}) from locality principles, and to extract universal data like the a-anomaly from the partition function.
AI.method: The authors use locality of the thermal effective action to derive analyticity constraints on ln Z at all orders in the high-temperature expansion. From these they derive infinite sets of sharp algebraic relations among expansion coefficients (homogeneous except at β¹ order due to the Weyl anomaly), and show the relations resum into differential equations in β in the fast-spinning (ω_i → 1) limit. They verify against various CFTs and generalize to arbitrary even d, demonstrating absence of analogous relations in odd d.
AI.result: An infinite system of homogeneous relations constraining the high-temperature expansion coefficients of the CFT free energy is derived, with the a-anomaly extractable from the partition function. The relations are verified in multiple CFT examples and hold for all even dimensions but not odd dimensions.
AI.conclusion: Locality of the thermal effective action is a powerful organizing principle that fully determines the analytic structure of the high-temperature/fast-rotation expansions of the CFT partition function in even dimensions, linking it to the Weyl anomaly.

title: Strong Constraints for Line Signals from Dark Matter Annihilation in Sub-halo
summary: We present a dedicated search for monochromatic gamma-ray emission from a recently proposed nearby dark matter subhalo candidate. Using nearly 15 years of Fermi-LAT Pass 8 data, we perform a sliding-window search for gamma-ray lines between 10 and 300 GeV. We do not find any statistically significant evidence for a line signal. The largest excess occurs at $E_γ\simeq 28 \, {\rm GeV}$ with a local significance of $2.5σ$. We therefore derive 95% confidence level upper limits on the annihilation cross section for $χχ\rightarrow γγ$. Under the assumed NFW subhalo model, the resulting constraints are stronger than existing Galactic Center line limits over much of the explored mass range. We further translate these line constraints into bounds on well-motivated WIMP models, such as Higgs-portal and Wino dark matter scenarios, restricting previously open parameter regions consistent with thermal freeze-out as well as models associated with dark matter interpretations of the Galactic Center Excess.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a dedicated search for monochromatic gamma-ray lines from a nearby dark matter subhalo candidate using ~15 years of Fermi-LAT Pass 8 data, finding no significant signal (largest excess at 28 GeV with 2.5σ local significance) and deriving 95% confidence level upper limits on the annihilation cross section for χχ→γγ. These constraints are stronger than Galactic Center line limits over much of the explored mass range and restrict parameter space in Higgs-portal and Wino dark matter models, including regions consistent with thermal freeze-out and Galactic Center Excess interpretations.
AI.motivation: To search for gamma-ray line signals from a nearby dark matter subhalo candidate, which could provide complementary and potentially more sensitive constraints than traditional Galactic Center searches, thereby testing well-motivated WIMP dark matter scenarios.
AI.method: Using nearly 15 years of Fermi-LAT Pass 8 data, the authors perform a sliding-window search for gamma-ray lines between 10 and 300 GeV toward a recently proposed nearby dark matter subhalo candidate. Limits are derived under an assumed NFW subhalo density profile, and results are translated into constraints on specific WIMP models including Higgs-portal and Wino dark matter.
AI.result: No statistically significant line signal is found. The largest excess occurs at Eγ~28 GeV with a local significance of 2.5σ. The derived 95% CL upper limits on the annihilation cross section for χχ→γγ are stronger than existing Galactic Center line limits over much of the explored mass range, and the constraints exclude previously open parameter regions in Higgs-portal and Wino dark matter models.
AI.conclusion: The subhalo-targeted search approach provides competitive or superior constraints on dark matter annihilation into gamma-ray lines compared to Galactic Center analyses. The absence of a signal restricts parameter space for thermal freeze-out WIMP models and dark matter interpretations of the Galactic Center Excess, though no new line detection is reported.

title: Holographic zeros and poles from apparent singularities
summary: We study general holographic fluctuation equations with apparent singularities, and the associated spectral functions. We consider the regime where an apparent singularity approaches the boundary, for which the near-boundary behavior of solutions can be determined via an inner/outer matching type of calculation. Depending on properties of the equation, we find that the merging of an apparent singularity with the boundary may generate either a zero or a pole for the corresponding spectral function. Our results also indicate that the recently introduced holographic product formula still applies in the presence of apparent singularities.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes general holographic fluctuation equations with apparent singularities and their associated spectral functions, focusing on the regime where an apparent singularity approaches the boundary. Using inner/outer matching calculations, the authors show that the merging of an apparent singularity with the boundary can generate either a zero or a pole in the spectral function depending on equation properties. The holographic product formula is shown to remain valid even with apparent singularities present.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical implications of apparent singularities in holographic fluctuation equations, particularly how their behavior near the boundary affects spectral functions, and to verify the robustness of the holographic product formula when apparent singularities are present.
AI.method: The authors study general holographic fluctuation equations containing apparent singularities and employ an inner/outer matching type of calculation to determine the near-boundary behavior of solutions in the regime where an apparent singularity approaches the boundary.
AI.result: The merging of an apparent singularity with the boundary can generate either a zero or a pole in the corresponding spectral function, depending on the properties of the equation. Additionally, the holographic product formula continues to apply in the presence of apparent singularities.
AI.conclusion: The behavior of spectral functions in holographic theories is significantly affected by apparent singularities near the boundary, leading to either zeros or poles, yet the holographic product formula remains a valid tool even in this more general setting.

title: Energy-Energy Correlators in $Z$-Tagged Jets in $pp$ Collisions
summary: We present predictions for the collinear energy-energy correlator (EEC) measured inside $Z$-tagged jets in proton-proton collisions across the confinement transition. Our framework combines transverse-momentum-dependent factorization for back-to-back $Z+$jet production with an exclusive differential EEC jet function incorporating perturbative evolution and flavor-dependent non-perturbative fragmentation. The EEC jet function is evaluated at $\mathrm{NLL}^{\prime}$ accuracy, with separate quark and gluon non-perturbative scales constrained by existing $e^+e^-$ and inclusive-jet data. We provide predictions for forward $Z+$jet production at $\sqrt{s}=8~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $13~\mathrm{TeV}$ in the jet transverse-momentum intervals $(20, 30)$, $(30, 50)$ and $(50, 100) \, \mathrm{GeV}$. The EEC distributions as functions of $z_χ$ exhibit finite plateaus at small $z_χ$, while the corresponding angular distributions display the characteristic turnover associated with the confinement transition. A flavor decomposition shows that this transition becomes increasingly dominated by quark-initiated jets as the jet transverse momentum increases. Forward $Z$-tagged jets therefore provide a clean probe of non-perturbative quark fragmentation and offer a direct test of whether the characteristic confinement scale extracted from $e^+e^-$ collisions remains universal in a hadronic environment.

AI.tldr: This paper presents theoretical predictions for the collinear energy-energy correlator (EEC) measured inside Z-tagged jets in proton-proton collisions across the confinement transition, using TMD factorization combined with an NLL'-accurate differential EEC jet function that incorporates flavor-dependent non-perturbative fragmentation. The framework is applied to forward Z+jet production at 8 and 13 TeV, revealing finite plateaus at small z_chi and characteristic confinement-transition turnovers, with quark-initiated jets increasingly dominating the transition as jet pT increases.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the characteristic confinement scale extracted from e+e- collisions remains universal when probed in a hadronic environment (pp collisions), and to provide a clean probe of non-perturbative quark fragmentation using forward Z-tagged jets.
AI.method: Combines transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization for back-to-back Z+jet production with an exclusive differential EEC jet function. The EEC jet function is evaluated at NLL' accuracy, with separate quark and gluon non-perturbative scales constrained by existing e+e- and inclusive-jet data. Predictions are made for forward Z+jet production at sqrt(s)=8 and 13 TeV across three jet pT intervals.
AI.result: The EEC distributions as functions of z_chi exhibit finite plateaus at small z_chi, while angular distributions display the characteristic turnover associated with the confinement transition. Flavor decomposition shows the transition becomes increasingly dominated by quark-initiated jets as jet transverse momentum increases.
AI.conclusion: Forward Z-tagged jets provide a clean probe of non-perturbative quark fragmentation and offer a direct test of whether the confinement scale extracted from e+e- collisions is universal in a hadronic environment.

title: Monstrous parafermionic defects and other non-invertible symmetries in chiral CFTs
summary: The structure of non-invertible symmetries in 2D CFT is closely tied to the algebra of preserved holomorphic fields, its representation theory, and its embedding in the full chiral algebra of the CFT. Unfortunately, finding new embeddings of a chiral algebra into another is a difficult mathematical problem, and one of the major obstacles in the pursue of new and exotic categories of non-invertible symmetries. In this work, we describe a simple general technique that leads to a number of new non-trivial results in this direction: (1) For the holomorphic Monster CFT $V^\natural$, we show that for every `Fricke' non-anomalous Monster element of order $N$, there is an embedding of the parafermion algebra $\frac{su(2)_N}{u(1)}$ in $V^\natural$, we compute the characters of its commutant, and describe the topological defects preserving these subalgebras. (2) We provide an easy-to-check sufficient condition for a holomorphic VOA $V$ to be self-orbifold under a cyclic group of (invertible) symmetries, and determine the associated duality defect. (3) We find several new topological defects in CFTs arising from heterotic strings on $T^4$. (4) We prove a number of VOA embeddings and topological defects in the Leech lattice CFT, in Schellekens theories, and other CFTs of various central charges, and suggest several generalizations of our methods.

It yields new embeddings of parafermion algebras into the Monster CFT, criteria for self-orbifolds of holomorphic VOAs, new topological defects in heterotic string CFTs, and various VOA embeddings in Leech lattice and Schellekens theories.

However, finding new embeddings of a chiral algebra into another is mathematically difficult, and this difficulty obstructs the discovery of new and exotic categories of non-invertible symmetries.

title: Quark Mixing Model with Three Higgs Doublets and $S_3$ Modular Symmetry at $τ=i$
summary: We study the quark sector of a model with three Higgs electroweak doublets, complemented with a modular $S_3$ symmetry. We show that a proper assignment of the quark and Higgs fields in $S_3$ and their modular weights allows to write a mass matrix with a phenomenologically viable texture. Moreover, by considering the conditions on the Higgs VEVs derived from the minimization of the scalar potential together with evaluation of the Yukawa couplings at the fixed point $τ=i$, leads to a significant reduction of the free parameters. We present two setups, one with three effective parameters, which is overly constrained, and one with four effective parameters, where the $V_{CKM}$ matrix can be fitted precisely.

By imposing scalar-potential minimization conditions on Higgs VEVs and evaluating Yukawa couplings at the fixed point τ=i, the free parameters are significantly reduced. Two setups are presented: one with three effective parameters (overly constrained) and one with four effective parameters where V_CKM can be fitted precisely.

title: The trans-Planckian problem and gravitational interactions
comment: 20 pages, 2 figures; contribution to Comptes Rendus. Physique - a special issue in memory of Renaud Parentani (the typesetting is more elegant in the Comptes Rendus version)
summary: The strong gravitational interaction of counter-propagating quantum field modes is of foundational importance to the trans-Planckian problem of black hole horizons. This article, in memory of Renaud Parentani, is primarily an exposition of Renaud's attempt, using perturbation theory, a large $N$ approximation, and spherical reduction, to capture a mechanism by which those interactions might quench the trans-Planckian near-horizon quantum field correlations. Before giving a detailed account of Renaud's calculation, the trans-Planckian problem is briefly introduced, and the paper concludes with a discussion of related issues and questions.

title: Statistical Symmetry Breaking and Emergent Colored Noise in a Stochastic Scalar-Doublet Field Theory
summary: We investigate a relativistic stochastic field theory in which a complex scalar doublet is coupled to a complex white-noise source. The action preserves Lorentz and $\mathrm{U(1)}\times\mathrm{SU(2)}$ symmetries at the statistical level, whereas the corresponding Euler-Lagrange equations exhibit symmetry breaking along individual stochastic realizations. Within a gauge-field-free sector introduced to obtain analytical solutions, we show that the scalar doublet undergoes a noise-driven random walk in field space, leading to a finite, time-dependent ensemble average of its magnitude. As an illustrative application, we further investigate the coupling of the stochastic scalar field to fermions through a Yukawa interaction. The scalar-field solution naturally separates into a tail component, which contributes as an effective mass-like term, and a light-cone component, which acts as a colored-noise source that induces a spatially correlated stochastic phase in the fermion wave function. The statistical properties and correlation length of this emergent colored noise are derived analytically within the adopted approximations. The present work provides an exploratory study of statistical symmetry breaking and emergent colored-noise dynamics in a relativistic stochastic scalar-doublet field theory.

The action preserves Lorentz and U(1)×SU(2) symmetries statistically, but individual stochastic realizations break these symmetries in the Euler-Lagrange equations. Coupling to fermions via Yukawa interaction yields a two-component solution: a tail component acting as an effective mass, and a light-cone component serving as colored noise that induces spatially correlated stochastic phases in the fermion wave function. Analytical results for the emergent colored-noise statistics and correlation length are derived.

They restrict to a gauge-field-free sector to obtain analytical solutions, solve the stochastic equations of motion for the scalar field, and derive the statistical properties of the solution. title: Boundary-Value Problem in Type IIB Supergravity and Holography
summary: In precision holography, the Euclidean on-shell action of type IIB supergravity often fails to reproduce the leading large-$N$ free energy of the dual field theory: the type IIB pseudo action, for instance, vanishes identically on the $\mathrm{EAdS}_5\times S^5$ background. We address this issue by revisiting the boundary-value problem of the Euclidean type IIB pseudo action from first principles. Classifying the admissible boundary conditions through the variational principle, we construct a generalized pseudo action whose boundary terms implement the choice of ensemble --- fixed potentials versus fixed quantized Page charges --- in which the holographic comparison is performed. For the fixed five-form-charge ensemble, the resulting boundary term reproduces the recently proposed topological correction to the Pasti--Sorokin--Tonin formulation of type IIB supergravity for holographic backgrounds of interest. We then test the generalized pseudo action on two complementary backgrounds: the $\mathrm{EAdS}_3\times S^3\times M_4$ near-horizon geometry of the D1-D5 system and the warped $\mathrm{EAdS}_6\times S^2\timesΣ$ solutions dual to five-dimensional SCFTs. In both cases the ten-dimensional on-shell action agrees exactly with that of the corresponding lower-dimensional supergravity, and thereby with the leading large-$N$ free energy of the dual SCFT. Our results establish the choice of boundary conditions --- and hence of ensemble --- as an essential ingredient of precision holography directly in type IIB supergravity, extending recent analyses in eleven-dimensional supergravity.

This boundary term reproduces the known topological correction to the Pasti–Sorokin–Tonin formulation for holographic backgrounds. The generalized action is tested on EAdS3×S3×M4 (D1-D5) and warped EAdS6×S2×Σ backgrounds, where the ten-dimensional on-shell action exactly matches the lower-dimensional supergravity actions and hence the leading large-N free energies of the dual SCFTs. title: Leading-Neutron Electroproduction at HERA and the EIC: Sullivan Process, Target Fragmentation, and Pion PDFs
summary: Leading-neutron electroproduction measurements from the H1 and ZEUS experiments at HERA have been used to constrain pion parton distribution functions (PDFs) at small momentum fractions within the Sullivan one-pion-exchange (OPE) framework, complementing large-$x_π$ constraints from pion-induced Drell--Yan measurements. Previous analyses have focused primarily on the region of large neutron longitudinal momentum fraction, $x_L$, where contributions from deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) target fragmentation are suppressed. In this work, we use the \textsc{Pythia} event generator to model the target-fragmentation contribution and show that its combination with the OPE contribution reproduces the main features of the HERA leading-neutron data over the full measured $x_L$ range without introducing additional ad hoc normalization factors. This result demonstrates the potential of incorporating a broader range of leading-neutron data into future global analyses, thereby extending sensitivity to smaller pion momentum fractions $x_π$. We investigate the model dependence associated with the pion--nucleon vertex form factor and show that the HERA data are sensitive to different target-fragmentation treatments implemented in \textsc{Pythia}. Finally, we present projections for leading-neutron production at the future U.S. Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), identifying beam-energy configurations and kinematic regions that provide enhanced sensitivity to pion structure while suppressing DIS target-fragmentation contributions.

The authors investigate model dependence from the pion-nucleon vertex form factor, and provide projections for future EIC measurements with optimized beam-energy configurations and kinematic regions.

This limits sensitivity to small pion momentum fractions x_pi, and excludes a substantial portion of available data. The authors aim to remove this restriction by explicitly modeling the target-fragmentation background.

This is combined with the Sullivan one-pion-exchange (OPE) framework contribution to reproduce HERA leading-neutron data across the full measured x_L range. Model dependence is assessed by varying the pion-nucleon vertex form factor treatment and different target-fragmentation implementations in Pythia. Forward projections are made for the EIC.

HERA data show sensitivity to different target-fragmentation treatments in Pythia and to the pion-nucleon form factor. Projections identify EIC beam-energy configurations and kinematic regions with enhanced sensitivity to pion structure and suppressed fragmentation backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating broader ranges of leading-neutron data into future global fits is viable, extending sensitivity to smaller x_pi values. The approach paves the way for refined pion PDF extraction, and the EIC projections suggest optimal running conditions for future measurements of pion structure.

title: Conical Defects in JT Gravity from BF Theory: Quantization, Fusion, and Weighted Moduli Spaces
summary: We construct a gauge-invariant BF representative of a conical defect in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity, with its elliptic direction fixed by the reconstruction of the gravitational variables. In the gravitational sector, the BF observable reproduces the metric defect insertion and its distributional curvature source, and fixes the holonomy around the defect to an elliptic conjugacy class. For a single defect on the disk, the position integral combines with the residual \(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb R)\) quotient, leaving a fixed elliptic sector. The exact boundary quantization of this sector gives the elementary kernel and one-defect disk amplitude directly, without using a matrix model. The same local BF operator describes both sharp and blunt defects. Their difference appears only when several defect positions are integrated. BF source composition makes the fractional deficits additive. Requiring a fused source to remain in the gravitational cone sector gives the admissibility condition for defect collisions, while positivity of the hyperbolic area on each component gives the corresponding stability condition. These conditions coincide with those for Hassett weighted curves. Combining these BF results with the known Hassett compactification and conical Weil--Petersson geometry yields the fixed-order genus-zero contact terms and recovers the cluster expansion of deformed JT gravity. Thus sharp and blunt defects differ through the compactified geometry of their relative positions, rather than through the elementary BF operator.

The distinction between them emerges only when integrating over multiple defect positions, governed by fusion/admissibility/stability conditions that coincide with Hassett weighted curve conditions. Combining BF results with Hassett compactification and conical Weil–Petersson geometry yields fixed-order genus-zero contact terms and recovers the cluster expansion of deformed JT gravity.

The elliptic holonomy is fixed around the defect, and on a single-defect disk the position integral combines with the residual PSL(2,R) quotient leaving a fixed elliptic sector whose exact boundary quantization gives the elementary kernel and one-defect disk amplitude. BF source composition makes fractional deficits additive; requiring fused sources to remain in the gravitational cone sector yields admissibility conditions for defect collisions, while hyperbolic-area positivity per component gives stability conditions. These are identified with Hassett weighted curve conditions, and combined with conical Weil–Petersson geometry to get genus-zero contact terms and deformed JT cluster expansion.

Exact boundary quantization directly yields the elementary kernel and one-defect disk amplitude without a matrix model. The Hassett conditions naturally govern admissible defect fusion and stability, yielding consistency with deformed JT gravity contact terms and cluster expansions.

title: Meson mass spectrum in isospin QCD medium from the $N_f=2+1$ quark-meson model
summary: We study phase structures, meson mass spectra, and sound velocities at finite temperature and density in QCD with isospin chemical potential ($μ_I$). We employ the quark-meson model with $N_f=2+1$, incorporating the Kobayashi-Maskawa-'t Hooft type coupling to capture dynamical effects of the $U(1)_A$ axial anomaly. Within the mean-field approximation at quark one-loop, we analyze the onset of pion condensation, which manifests as a second-order phase transition at low temperatures and may exhibit a first-order behavior at higher temperatures within this approximation. We examine the corresponding mass spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar singlet-octet mesons, in which the $π_+$ mass is exactly massless in the superfluid phase due to its Nambu-Goldstone boson nature. The neutral pion mass is, meanwhile, found to exhibit a strictly linear growth with $μ_I$ in the pion condensed phase. We also investigate the isothermal squared sound velocity and identify characteristic structures associated with the phase transitions. Furthermore, we highlight how enhanced $U(1)_A$ anomaly effects facilitate the pion condensate to generate a less-pronounced sound velocity peak in cold medium. Our findings are expected to provide future lattice simulations with useful information on meson mass spectra from symmetry aspects.

AI.tldr: This paper studies QCD at finite temperature and isospin chemical potential using a 2+1 flavor quark-meson model with Kobayashi-Maskawa-'t Hooft coupling. Within mean-field at one-loop, it analyzes pion condensation phase transitions, scalar/pseudoscalar meson mass spectra, and isothermal sound velocities, revealing exact masslessness of the π+ (NG boson) in the superfluid phase, strictly linear growth of neutral pion mass with μ_I, and how enhanced U(1)_A anomaly effects suppress sound velocity peaks in cold media.
AI.motivation: To understand phase structures, meson mass spectra, and sound velocities in QCD matter at finite temperature and isospin chemical potential, particularly the role of pion condensation and the U(1)_A axial anomaly, which has implications for both strong-interaction theory and future lattice simulations.
AI.method: The authors employ the N_f=2+1 quark-meson model with Kobayashi-Maskawa-'t Hooft type coupling to include U(1)_A axial anomaly effects. The analysis is performed within the mean-field approximation at quark one-loop level, tracking pion condensation onset, meson mass spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar singlet-octet states, and isothermal squared sound velocities.

The neutral pion mass grows strictly linearly with μ_I in the condensed phase. The isothermal squared sound velocity exhibits characteristic structures tied to the phase transitions, and stronger U(1)_A anomaly effects cause a less-pronounced sound velocity peak in cold medium.
AI.conclusion: The findings clarify how pion condensation and the U(1)_A anomaly affect meson spectra and hydrodynamic properties at finite μ_I, and are expected to offer useful benchmark information from symmetry aspects for future lattice QCD simulations.

title: Center-twisted Gribov spectra and the finite-volume Gaussian response in the refined Gribov--Zwanziger framework
summary:
We develop a continuum framework for comparing the Gribov--Zwanziger and center-vortex descriptions of confinement through the gauge-invariant twisted partition function of the electric $\mathbb{Z}_N^{[1]}$ 1-form symmetry. A background 2-form field $B$, equivalently an 't~Hooft twist on a torus, labels a global sector and is not itself a dynamical center vortex.
  For a minimal irreducible twist on $T^4$, we derive the complete adjoint momentum lattice of $SU(N)$. The twisted spectrum is exactly the scalar spectrum on an enlarged torus with periods $(L_1,L_2,NL_3,NL_4)$ with the ordinary-torus sublattice removed. This yields a finite Faddeev--Popov gap at the flat representative and reduces twisted-minus-untwisted spectral traces to ordinary torus traces. For the refined Gribov--Zwanziger (RGZ) kernel, Poisson resummation gives an exact finite-volume Bessel-function winding sum with a universal center-twist projector.
  We evaluate the Gaussian one-loop integral at fixed RGZ parameters up to the finite-dimensional global zero-mode/stabilizer normalization. The Zwanziger determinants cancel, while the gauge-fixing/ghost sector leaves a universal massless primed determinant on $T^4$; the untwisted sector also contains constant gluon modes. The only normalization not fixed by the local quadratic Hessian is the relative zero-mode/stabilizer measure of the reducible untwisted and irreducibly twisted flat connections. We also derive closed finite-volume sources for the RGZ stationary equations.
  The massive response is exponentially suppressed at large volume, whereas the massless factor depends on the global zero-mode normalization. Thus the Gaussian calculation does not by itself establish the strong center-vortex-condensation criterion for $Z[B]/Z[0]$, but it isolates the remaining global normalization problem and separates a global twist from an actual dynamical vortex.

After Poisson resummation and Gaussian one-loop evaluation, massive contributions decay exponentially with volume while massless factors depend on an unresolved global zero-mode/stabilizer normalization, so the calculation does not by itself establish the strong center-vortex-condensation criterion but cleanly separates a global twist from a dynamical vortex.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to systematically compare two prominent but distinct descriptions of confinement—the Gribov-Zwanziger mechanism and the center-vortex picture—within a single gauge-invariant continuum framework, using the twisted partition function of the electric 1-form center symmetry as the common object of study.

title: Exploring millicharged particles in laboratory and astrophysical strong-field regimes
summary: The probe of light dark particles beyond the Standard Model (SM) under a strong-field environment has drawn significant attention. In this work, we investigate the potential to search for and constrain light millicharged particles (MCPs) via strong electromagnetic fields in both laboratory laser experiments and astrophysical environments such as magnetars. We propose the MCP pair production from nonlinear Compton scattering through the interaction of a relativistic electron beam with a high-intensity laser pulse. The Furry picture and Volkov solution of Dirac equation in a background electromagnetic field are used to describe the electrons and MCPs under an external classical laser field. We calculate the cross sections of nonlinear Compton scattering to MCP pairs and take into account the irreducible SM background with missing neutrinos. We also revisit the MCP pair production via the Schwinger mechanism from magnetars with ultra-strong magnetic field and parallel electric field in polar gap. The energy loss due to the Schwinger pair production of MCPs and electric field acceleration is evaluated based on Ruderman-Sutherland model for confirmed magnetars. We find that the constraints from highly magnetized magnetars and the search potential in laboratory laser experiments are complementary.

Complementary constraints are found between magnetar observations and laboratory laser experiments.

Calculates cross sections for MCP pair production via nonlinear Compton scattering, accounts for irreducible SM background from missing neutrinos, and revisits Schwinger pair production of MCPs from magnetars based on the Ruderman-Sutherland model by evaluating energy loss from MCP pair production and electric field acceleration.

title: Topics in Kadyshevsky Field Theory
summary: In these notes we deal with several field theoretical topics in the framework of the Quantum Field Theory as developed by Kadyshevsky. The main motivation for studying the Kadyshevsky formalism is that in the kadyshevsky graphs, in contrast with the Feynman graphs, the particles remain on the mass shell. This facilitates the use of phenomenological form factors, {\it e.g.} Gaussian ones. In the first part we construct the second quantised quasi-particle formalism, which is employed to develop the functional integral formalism. In the latter we develop the path-integral, the Schwinger-Symanzik equations, generalised Wightman functions, and the Kadyshevsky reduction formulas. In the second part we cover the topics: (i) the relation between the Feynman and Kadyshevsky perturbation theory, and (ii) the Gross-Jackiw method in the Kadyshevsky formalism. The latter method is applied to the kadyshevsky formalism for interaction Lagrangians with derivatives, in particular for pion-nucleon interactions: (i) pseudo-vector $NNπ$-, (ii) vector $NNρ$-, and (iii) gauge-invariant $Δ_{33}Nπ$ coupling.

AI.tldr: This paper develops the Kadyshevsky formalism of Quantum Field Theory, where particles remain on the mass shell in graphs (unlike Feynman graphs), enabling the use of phenomenological form factors. It constructs second-quantized quasi-particle and functional integral formalisms, develops path-integrals, Schwinger-Symanzik equations, generalized Wightman functions, and Kadyshevsky reduction formulas, and explores the relation between Feynman and Kadyshevsky perturbation theory along with the Gross-Jackiw method applied to derivative interaction Lagrangians (pseudo-vector NNπ, vector NNρ, and gauge-invariant Δ33Nπ couplings).

title: CGC-py: A Monte Carlo Event Generator for Gluon Saturation Physics

summary: We develop CGC-py, a Monte Carlo event generator for deep-inelastic scattering. The predicted nuclear modification factor $R_{e\mathrm{Au}}^h$ shows the expected saturation pattern: suppression at low $p_T^*$ followed by a rise toward unity at higher $p_T^*$. A comparison with a \textsc{Pythia}~6 baseline, together with an $x_g$-rescaling study, indicates that small-$x$ CGC evolution and collinear DGLAP dynamics contribute comparably to the growth of the dihadron away-side width with energy. title: Quasi-local form for $α$--$z$ Rényi QNEC from fixed-ray escorts
summary: The fixed-ray escort integral representation expresses $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence as an average over ordinary relative entropy of a family of escort states. Working in the standard UV-regulated density-matrix description of QFT subregions, we use this representation to derive an escort-averaged entanglement first law, an escort-averaged representation of the $α$--$z$ information kernel, and an escort-averaged Bekenstein-type bound for ball-shaped regions in conformal field theories. For the conjectural $α$--$z$ quantum null energy condition (QNEC), we obtain a quasi-local form in which the null energy is evaluated in an escort-averaged state and is corrected by an escort-transport term encoding the failure of escort formation to commute with restriction to a null-deformed region. The $z=α$ specialization gives a similar quasi-local form of the Rényi QNEC for sandwiched Rényi divergence. We explicitly compute the Rényi QNEC, including the explicit escort transport term, for coherent-state excitations in a free scalar field theory. For the same coherent family, we obtain a positive $α$--$z$ null Hessian, verifying the conjectured diagonal $α$--$z$ QNEC for this family.

For z=α, this gives a quasi-local Rényi QNEC for sandwiched Rényi divergence, which is explicitly computed for coherent states in free scalar field theory, along with verifying a positive α–z null Hessian for the diagonal QNEC.

title: A Bayesian Pixel Based Approach for Model Independent TMD Reconstruction

summary: We introduce a nonparametric pixel-based framework for the Bayesian inference and imaging of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) parton distributions. title: Cusped Defects: Cusp Operator Expansion, Conformal Properties and Bootstrap Applications
summary: We analyze general properties of cusped defect lines embedded in generic conformal field theories (CFTs). These findings are checked and exemplified in the case of the localized magnetic field defect. Finally, we derive analytic constraints on dynamical cusp data by making use of a crossing equation, and discuss possible numerical bootstrap applications of our results.

title: Light Leptoquarks in a Dark Sector: Scalar Dark Matter, Neutrino Mass, and Collider Signatures
summary: We investigate the dark matter (DM) phenomenology and subsequent collider signatures of a dark leptoquark (LQ) model containing dark vector-like quarks (VLQs) and a scalar singlet. The dark LQs and VLQs participate in the radiative generation of Majorana neutrino masses at one loop. Since the coloured LQs and VLQs cannot serve as viable DM candidates, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd singlet scalar is introduced as the DM candidate. The $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd nature of the LQs forbids their conventional decays into a quark and a lepton, allowing them to evade the standard LHC constraints that apply to visible LQ signatures. This framework therefore offers the distinctive possibility of sub-TeV dark LQs coexisting with TeV-scale dark VLQs. These sub-TeV dark LQs help in achieving the observed relic abundance of the singlet through co-annihilation. We analyse the resulting DM phenomenology and assess the prospects for probing this scenario at a future muon collider.

title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
summary: An illuminating probe of the dynamics of a line defect is the global geometry of its worldline. For a conformal line defect in a conformal field theory, sharp corners in the worldline, i.e. cusps, host dynamical degrees of freedom characterized in part by a spectrum of scaling dimensions, called cusp anomalous dimensions. We present various general bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions following from unitarity and cutting-and-gluing consistency of different defect geometries. We first establish, for cusps involving conjugate defects, that level crossings upon varying the cusp angle are forbidden between the lightest singlet cusp and any non-singlet cusp, proving that singlet cusps are the lightest. Then, we study line defects arranged in a rectangular geometry, which are subject to bootstrap constraints reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap. We find an analytic ``magic" functional that produces an optimal and universal lower bound on the dimension of a right angle bare cusp in terms of the universal defect Casimir energy between the corresponding defect and its conjugate in flat space.

It proves singlet cusps are the lightest by forbidding level crossings with non-singlet cusps, and develops an analytic "magic" functional that yields an optimal universal lower bound on right-angle cusp dimensions in terms of the defect Casimir energy.

Establishing universal constraints on this spectrum from fundamental principles (unitarity and bootstrap consistency) helps understand defect dynamics without detailed model-specific computations.

They analyze level crossings between the lightest singlet cusp and non-singlet cusps for conjugate defects, and map rectangular defect configurations to a bootstrap problem reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap, where an analytic "magic" functional is constructed.

title: Probing the Geometry of Viable Froggatt-Nielsen-like Flavor Textures
summary: We investigate the geometry of viable Froggatt--Nielsen-like flavor textures in a controlled toy landscape. In this first texture-level analysis, each point is represented by the eighteen integer exponents entering the up- and down-type Yukawa matrices, without imposing the additional charge-factorization constraints of specific Froggatt--Nielsen models. Viability is imposed through cuts on quark mass ratios and selected CKM observables. We construct four benchmark ensembles, ranging from masses-only constraints to the inclusion of the full set of CKM observables considered in this work, and study the resulting point clouds in the raw exponent space. Principal-component analysis shows no evidence for strong linear compression: in all benchmarks, fifteen principal components are required to account for 90% of the variance. Nearest-neighbour intrinsic-dimensionality diagnostics, including TwoNN and Levina--Bickel estimators, support the same qualitative conclusion, yielding high effective dimensions of order 10-12. These results do not rule out hidden flavor-theory geometry in other coordinates; rather, they suggest that raw Froggatt--Nielsen exponents may not provide natural coordinates for revealing such a geometry.

title: SCFT/VOA correspondence and R-twisted reductions of $(A_2,D_{3n-2})$ Argyres--Douglas theories
summary: We study the SCFT/VOA correspondence for the $(A_2,D_{3n-2})$ Argyres--Douglas theories with $n\geq2$. From the matching of the central charges and the equality of the Schur index with the vacuum supercharacter to all orders, we propose that the associated VOA is the logarithmic doublet algebra $\mathcal A(4n-2)$ of Feigin, Feigin, and Tipunin. For $n=2$, this correspondence was studied in detail by Buican and Nishinaka, and our proposal extends it to $n\geq3$. Using the Nahm sum expression for the vacuum supercharacter, we further propose a family of 3d $\mathcal N=2$ abelian Chern--Simons matter theories that flow to the 3d $\mathcal N=4$ SCFTs obtained by the R-twisted circle reduction, generalizing the $n=2$ construction. We determine the monopole superpotential and show that the Coulomb branch is $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_2$ for every $n$. The superconformal index provides quantitative evidence for the proposed infrared fixed points, including the expected enhancement to $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetry and the Higgs and Coulomb branch structure.

title: Exploring Extended Higgs Dynamics via Higgsstrahlung at FCC-ee
summary: The Future Circular Electron-Positron Collider (FCC-ee) will probe aspects of the Higgs boson and the electroweak scale with unprecedented precision via associated Higgs production with a $Z$ boson. We demonstrate that the projected precision of the FCC-ee's 240 GeV run will enable a precise analysis of Beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM)-relevant Higgs-sector interactions near the alignment limit. As the key aspects of the 2HDM that drive deviations of the cross section from its Standard Model expectation (presence of new scalar states, Higgs mixing, and non-trivial inter-Higgs couplings) are also typically present in extensions more complex than the 2HDM, this demonstrates the FCC-ee's indirect potential for unveiling BSM physics around the electroweak scale.

title: The growth of $SO(9)$ super-representations in Type II string theory
summary: We study the growth of massive $SO(9)$ super-representations in type II and type I string theories. We do this first directly by finding an empirical formula that specifies which representations appear at any level, and then compute the multiplicities from a refined partition function evaluated over finite fields up to level 501 for individual representations, and level 226 for all representations. We then derive asymptotic formulae for the growth of any representation, which are constructed by integrating about the peaks of the refined partition function. Using a Rademacher sum we can find very accurate approximations for the multiplicities of the representations. Unlike the superstring partition function, which only receives contributions from the odd Rademacher terms, the multiplicities for any representation have contributions from both even and odd terms. Finally, we apply the same techniques to the ordinary representations, where a simplified refined partition function allows for better computational speed and simpler expressions for the asymptotic approximations.

title: TQ4Q2.0 Fragmentation Functions for Fully Heavy Tetraquark Production
comment: 7 pages, 1 figure. Proceedings of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: We investigate the fragmentation dynamics underlying the production of fully heavy tetraquarks by means of the TQ4Q2.0 collinear FF set, covering scalar ($0^{++}$), axial-vector ($1^{+-}$), and tensor ($2^{++}$) configurations. Attention is devoted to the axial-vector sector, whose fragmentation pattern makes it especially sensitive to intrinsic-charm contributions at LHC and FCC energies. title: Boundary conditions for axionic wormholes, imaginary distance bound and KSW allowability
summary: We study four-dimensional axion wormholes in the Lorentzian mini-superspace path integral using dual scalar and three-form flux formulations. We analyze this duality for generic metric boundary conditions and real lapse integration contour, and show that it holds on any background, including complex ones. With the Dirichlet condition on the metric, the fixed-flux path integral is evaluated exactly. In the Euclidean regime, saddle geometries organize into same-side and cross-throat segments of the Giddings-Strominger (GS) wormhole, depending on whether the two boundaries lie on the same or opposite sides of the throat. A Picard-Lefschetz analysis in the covering plane of lapse reveals that the cross-throat saddle has vanishing intersection number, and therefore does not contribute. In the asymptotically flat limit, it corresponds to the imaginary wormhole that saturates the imaginary distance bound (IDB). The same conclusion follows independently on the scalar side of the duality, and is confirmed by the exact amplitude. Replacing the Dirichlet condition with a one-parameter Neumann condition, the cross-throat saddle that leads to the imaginary wormholes remains irrelevant for the physical lift of the contour. title: Inelastic Signatures of Electroweak Dark Matter
summary: Minimal electroweak dark matter (DM) extended by a Majorana (M) and a Dirac (D) multiplet coupled through Higgs interactions provides a predictive framework for high-energy inelastic nuclear recoils. At the custodial point, electroweak symmetry breaking induces a neutral-state splitting $δ$ and an off-diagonal $Z$ interaction. For the coupled multiplets $3_M2_D$, $5_M4_D$, $7_M6_D$, $9_M8_D$, $11_M10_D$, and $13_M12_D$, both the splitting and the leading inelastic interaction are universal at fixed $(m_χ,y)$, independent of the electroweak representation. The observed high recoil energy points to splittings of a few hundred keV, while the fixed $Z$-mediated rate allows us to determine a mass-dependent $δ_{\rm LZ}(m_χ)$ by requiring one expected inelastic event in the LZ exposure, with a two-sided $90\%$ Poisson band. This defines a universal region in the $(m_χ,y)$ plane. Intersecting it with the representation-dependent thermal relic trajectories selects a benchmark for each multiplet. The corresponding electroweak representation then predicts a correlated loop-induced elastic spin-independent signal at lower recoil energies.

title: Baby-universe state dependence of the wormhole-induced gravi-axion mass gap
summary: Euclidean wormholes can break the axion shift symmetry, and when this symmetry is broken, a periodic potential is created for the axion, and the curvature of this potential at a minimum point can give the axion mass. In this work, we take seriously the assumption that the mere existence of a wormhole does not mean that the axion mass is uniquely determined, and that more information is needed to determine it. We first show that since for a Giddings--Strominger wormhole with symmetry \(O(4)\), the gravitational Pontryagin density is zero, the dynamical Chern--Simons interaction can affect quantum effects, including the determinant phase and fermionic selection rules, without changing the classical wormhole action. We also conclude that in a fixed \(α\) sector, the axion can have a specific mass, but this mass depends on the baby-universe state and is not a universal value. Then, for the mixed case of \(α\) sectors that give a distribution of conditional masses, we show that the lower edge of the averaged spectral measure is determined by the essential infimum of the conditional mass squared over the $α$ distribution. Finally, we conclude that even if almost all individual sectors are massive and the mean mass squared is also non-zero, if the support of the measure accumulates at the symmetric point \(α=0\), the averaged spectral measure will be gapless. To clarify the discussion, we consider a clear example of this situation, which can be a Gaussian baby-universe state, and show that in it the spectral threshold starts at zero and there is no isolated massive pole. Therefore, predicting the mass and cosmology of a gravi-axion from a wormhole without specifying the baby-universe state is not a unique, state-independent prediction.
